title: Income cutoff and subsidy program participation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD).

Rationale  
• Treatment (receipt of the housing subsidy) is assigned deterministically when household income is below a known threshold (running_var ≤ 0.5).  
• Households just on either side of the cutoff are assumed to be comparable except for treatment status, making local comparisons credible.

Key identifying assumptions  
1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of the subsidy, the conditional expectation of housing-expenditure share would evolve smoothly through the income cutoff.  
2. No precise manipulation: Households cannot perfectly sort their income to fall just below the eligibility line (checked with the McCrary density test).  
3. Correct functional form is approximated locally (addressed with local‐linear regression and bandwidth robustness).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ===== 0. Packages =====
required <- c("data.table", "ggplot2", "rdrobust", "rddensity")
installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for(p in setdiff(required, installed)) install.packages(p, quiet = TRUE)
lapply(required, library, character.only = TRUE)

# ===== 1. Read data =====
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s27_data.csv")

# ===== 2. Basic summary =====
cat("\nSample size:", nrow(df), "\n")

# ===== 3. McCrary density test (manipulation) =====
dens <- rddensity(df$running_var, c = 0.5)
cat("\nMcCrary (rddensity) log-difference in heights at cutoff:\n")
print(summary(dens))

# ===== 4. Main RDD estimate: local-linear with rdrobust =====
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = 0.5, p = 1)
cat("\nMAIN RESULT (local-linear, MSE-optimal bandwidth):\n")
print(summary(rd_main)$Estimate)

# Extract coefficient and CI
tau_hat  <- rd_main$Estimate[1,"coef"]
se_hat   <- rd_main$Estimate[1,"se"]
ci_low   <- rd_main$Estimate[1,"ci_lower"]
ci_high  <- rd_main$Estimate[1,"ci_upper"]
cat(sprintf("\nEstimated treatment effect at cutoff = %.4f (SE = %.4f; 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f])\n",
            tau_hat, se_hat, ci_low, ci_high))

# ===== 5. Robustness checks =====
## 5a. Different bandwidth (0.1)
rd_h01 <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = 0.5, h = 0.1, p = 1)
cat("\nRobustness: bandwidth = 0.10\n")
print(rd_h01$Estimate[1,])

## 5b. Larger bandwidth (0.20)
rd_h02 <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = 0.5, h = 0.2, p = 1)
cat("\nRobustness: bandwidth = 0.20\n")
print(rd_h02$Estimate[1,])

## 5c. Quadratic specification
rd_quad <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = 0.5, p = 2)
cat("\nRobustness: quadratic polynomial (p = 2)\n")
print(rd_quad$Estimate[1,])

## 5d. Placebo cutoff at 0.60 (should be ≈0)
placebo <- rdrobust(df$y, df$running_var, c = 0.6, p = 1)
cat("\nPlacebo cutoff at 0.60:\n")
print(placebo$Estimate[1,])

# ===== 6. Simple RD plot (optional, saved automatically) =====
ggplot(df, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "red") +
  geom_smooth(data = df[df$running_var <= 0.5], method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              formula = y ~ x, colour = "blue") +
  geom_smooth(data = df[df$running_var > 0.5],  method = "lm", se = FALSE,
              formula = y ~ x, colour = "green") +
  labs(title = "RDD: Housing expenditure share vs. Income ratio",
       x = "Income / threshold (running variable)",
       y = "Housing expenditure share") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("rdd_plot.png", width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 300)
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Eligibility for (and receipt of) a housing subsidy should relax the household’s budget constraint, allowing higher spending on housing; thus the jump in housing-expenditure share at the cutoff should be > 0.  

Magnitude: With a subsidy covering a modest portion of housing costs, a reasonable expectation is an increase of roughly 5–10 percentage points in the share of total expenditure devoted to housing (τ ≈ 0.05 – 0.10). A 95 % confidence interval that does not include zero and a null effect at the placebo cutoff would support causal interpretation.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — income cutoff; test for manipulation; local linear; optimal bandwidth (IK or CCT)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Eligible households increase housing expenditure share
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~25pp increase in housing spend for eligible households
